This is stated in their [Community Guidelines](https://sellercentral.amazon.com/gp/help/external/200336260) and [Review policies](https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html?ref_=help search 100336260). - The seller's behavior is ** not "gray area"**— it's a direct breach of rules designed to keep reviews honest. 100% positive reviews with 1,000+ ratings is a red flag for artificial inflation (a common tactic in these schemes). ### 2️️ **"WIBTA" is the wrong question** - "Would I be the asshole?" (WIBTA) frames this as a *personal moral judgment between you and the seller*. **It's not.** - This isn't about *your* relationship with the seller—it's about ** protecting Amazon's ecosystem**. - If *no one* reports this, the scam grows. - Fake reviews mislead *hundreds of other buyers* (e.g., someone might buy a defective product because they trust the 100% "positive" reviews). - **You're not " tattling"— you're being a responsible community member.** ### 3️️ **You did nothing wrong** - You ** did not leave a fake review** (as you confirmed). - You ** did not accept the free item *because* of a review** ( you didn't even pretend to leave one). - The seller *chose* to send you the free item anyway— that's on * them*, not you. - ** keeping the free item is not " being an asshole"— it's a byproduct of the seller's violation.** ### what you should do: - **Report the seller immediately** via Amazon: 1. Go to the seller's page on Amazon. 2. Click "Contact seller" or "Report abuse" ( usually under "Seller information"). 3. Say: * "This seller is offering free items in exchange for 5-star reviews, which violates Amazon's policies. I received a free item after they sent a note in the package ( see attached screenshot of their note) and their current packaging states '5-star review = free item' for all products. I did not leave a review for this or any of their products."* - **Attach screenshots** of: - The seller's note in the package. - The "5-star review = free item" message in the * second* package. - The seller's page showing their 1,000+ 100% positive reviews. - **Do not return the free item**— it's not your responsibility to " make it right" for their violation. Amazon will handle it. ### Why this matters: - ** Fake reviews cost real people money and safety.** A study by Harvard found that 1 in 10 Amazon reviews is fake. Scams like this make it harder to trust genuine feedback. - **Amazon * wants* you to report this.** They have a dedicated team to investigate these violations ( and they * do* ban sellers for it). - **You're not " being an asshole"— you're being a good citizen.** If everyone stayed silent, these schemes would dominate the platform. > ️ **Final note:** If you're worried about " being a snitch," remember: ** the seller is the one breaking the rules.** Reporting them is like calling the police if you see someone shoplifting— it's not " tattling," it's upholding the system that protects * everyone*. > **Do it.** Amazon will likely remove the seller's ability to sell on their platform. You'll have helped thousands of future buyers. 💡
